recommended_title: Memorization Without Observed Grokking Across MLP Widths
central_question: Within a fixed training horizon, how do hidden width and weight decay affect memorization and observed generalization in modular-arithmetic MLPs, and what can a censored width-lag contrast actually establish?
central_thesis: Across the tested modular addition and subtraction conditions, wider fixed-rate MLPs attain sustained memorization earlier or attain it when the narrowest models do not, yet none attains sustained generalization within 20,000 updates; the reported width-lag contrast therefore reflects memorization and endpoint substitution, not an identified effect on grokking time.
narrative_rationale: The final evidence supports a controlled, finite-horizon negative-results study across width and decay, augmented by an exact audit of the reported lag statistic. This is stronger than a proposed capacity-versus-decay-clock mechanism, which lacks the proposed random-label and calibration interventions, or a learning-rate-superiority story, which lacks a final-plane comparator. The scientific contribution is the observed separation between fitting and generalization plus the identification limit of capped lag, not a new optimizer or a universal claim about model scale. The original mechanistic question is only partially answered. Negative results support a coherent standalone paper, but readiness is not a prediction of ICLR acceptance.

method_groups.name: Fixed-rate MLP width family without weight decay
method_groups.include_reason: Widths 16, 64, and 256 at the frozen constant-rate recipe supply the within-final-evaluation reference for fitting times and held-out behavior in both operations. This is a scientific reference condition, not an unevaluated original-program comparison.

method_groups.name: Matched width family with unit weight decay
method_groups.include_reason: The same widths, operation-specific data, seed values, training horizon, and learning-rate recipe with AdamW decay 1 isolate the evaluated decay intervention conditional on this architecture and initialization scheme. The narrowest networks never attain the memorization threshold, unlike widths 64 and 256.

method_groups.name: Nonlearning prediction references
method_groups.include_reason: Stored initial-network, training-label-mode, exact-pair lookup with mode fallback, and label-deranged-input prediction accuracies contextualize low held-out accuracy. The lookup and mode references coincide because held-out pairs are disjoint. These are not separately trained random-label networks and are not a causal mechanism test.

results_focus: Lead with a width-by-decay comparison, split by addition and subtraction, rather than learning-rate search order. Use late-window training and held-out accuracy with individual seed observations; both operations are evidence blocks for one finite-horizon thesis, not separate discoveries.

Keep a main-text event table for all twelve operation/decay/width cells. Report all three observed memorization times or non-attainment, alongside generalization attainment counts. Widths 64 and 256 memorize at checkpoint 500 in every condition; width 16 without decay memorizes at 1000 or 1500; width 16 with decay never crosses. All 36 generalization events are unobserved.

Define memorization as training accuracy at least 0.99 and generalization as held-out accuracy at least 0.95 at three consecutive checkpoints. Checkpoints are 500 updates apart; event times are the first checkpoint of a qualifying triplet, not precisely resolved continuous crossing times. Delayed generalization requires both observed events and a positive lag.

Audit the capped-lag statistic explicitly. Its value is T when memorization is absent and max(0, (G if observed else T) - M) otherwise. For positive decay, the narrowest models receive T and width-256 models receive T-500, mechanically giving the reported 500-update contrast and [500, 500] interval. Report that interval faithfully as the supplied three-seed statistic, not as precision about unobserved generalization times.

The supplied decay interaction of 1083.3333333333335 updates is also an interaction of the capped statistic, not evidence that decay changes a generalization clock. The negative no-decay width contrast follows earlier memorization in larger networks while generalization is absent. Keep the algebra and the censoring caveat in the main paper.

Contextualize final held-out accuracy using stored nonlearning references. If the aggregate final accuracy or control gap is reported, define it in reader-facing units: the final-five-checkpoint mean and the equally weighted gap to four references, respectively. Do not treat the aggregate as superiority or compare it to search-plane aggregates.

Show seed values rather than relying on significance tests. There are three independent initialization seeds on a fixed split per operation; the twelve condition records within a seed are paired, not twelve independent replications. Zero observed generalization does not identify eventual event rates or support a pooled independent-binomial confidence interval.
figure_plan: Figure 1, early overview: the evaluated width-by-decay design, distinct memorization/generalization events, and the inference boundary imposed by a finite horizon. No invented learning curves or proposed unrun interventions.

Figure 2, main comparison: a 2-by-2 quantitative display of late-window training and held-out accuracy against width; columns are operations, rows are distinct accuracy metrics, colors encode decay, and seed points remain visible.

Figure 3, censoring audit: two direct-comparison panels, one per decay condition, showing capped lag versus width with operation-specific series and individual seeds. Explicitly label every generalization time as unobserved and explain the endpoint-substitution identity next to the figure.
